finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied Base64 data is passed to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via gadget chains.
finding.source: POST /restore form/query parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication required

trace.note: params[:state] is Base64-decoded and fed directly into Marshal.load
state.inspect is called on the deserialized object, which also triggers attacker-influenced methods

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, authorization, signature/HMAC check, class allowlist, or input validation on the path; the app is a single file with no before filters or middleware. Sinatra's default Rack::Protection does not prevent this (it is not CSRF-relevant for a direct attacker request).

verdict.reason: app.rb:6 passes Base64-decoded params[:state] straight into Marshal.load inside the unauthenticated `post "/restore"` route (app.rb:5), with no auth, signature, allowlist or filters in the single-file app (app.rb is the only file).
